newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala must probe rebel's death - Amnesty.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala must probe rebel's death - Amnesty.

text.p: Amnesty International urged Guatemala on Wednesday to investigate the disappearance of a rebel commander who might have been killed by state security forces.

"The Guatemalan government has one way to demonstrate its political will to combat impunity: the rapid and effective investigation of the presumed disappearance at the hands of security forces of Juan Jose Cabrera," the London-based human rights group said in a statement.

Cabrera and a guerrilla comrade Augusto Rafael Baldizon were involved in a high-profile kidnapping last year which violated the terms of a ceasefire in force at the time and deeply embarrassed the Guatemala National Revolutionary Unit (URNG) rebels.
In a rare show of unity, both the government and the rebels denied for weeks that he even existed.
Amnesty accused the government of "turning a deaf ear to repeated calls" to investigate Cabrera's disappearance.

The United Nations Mission for the Verification of Human Rights in Guatemala (MINUGUA) concluded on Tuesday that elite army officials illegally captured and probably killed Cabrera during the final round of peace talks last fall.
Guatemalan President Alvaro Arzu's office called MINUGUA's assertion unfounded and rejected its claim that government officials had stymied the investigation by withholding information.
Cabrera could be the last high-profile casualty in the URNG's 36-year armed rebellion that ended with the signing of an historic peace agreement on Dec. 29.
The URNG, which refused comment on Wednesday, is expected to release a statement on Thursday concerning the case.
More than 140,000 people were killed or disappeared during the country's civil war.
